title: EOS Org Chart Engine Specification
description: Complete org chart engine specification — department model, role model, hierarchy, default departments, template system, agent mapping, permissions, MVP scope, and end state

department_model.description: A department is a structural grouping within a company/entity that owns roles, metrics, workflows, and an AI agent. Departments are data entities persisted in the database, not prompt context. The canonical Pydantic model is substrate.types.Department.

venture_id.description: Specific venture/company within the org, if scoped

agent_name.description: Slug of the AI agent assigned to this department (e.g., 'eos-sales')

permission_tier.description: Department-level authority ceiling. One of: read, draft, execute, commit

roles.description: Role slugs that belong to this department (e.g., ['sales_lead', 'bdr', 'account_executive'])

metrics.description: KPI slugs tracked by this department (e.g., ['pipeline_value', 'conversion_rate'])

workflows.description: Workflow slugs owned by this department (e.g., ['outreach', 'follow_up', 'pipeline_review'])

active.description: Whether the department is currently active

metadata.description: Extensible metadata bag for department-specific config

role_model.description: A role is the atomic operating unit in the EOS hierarchy. Everything attaches to a role — a role can be operated by human, AI, or both. The role is the unit of authority, delegation, and performance measurement. The canonical Pydantic model is substrate.types.Role.

department.description: Department slug this role belongs to

venture_id.description: Specific venture/company within the org, if scoped

operator.description: Who operates this role — human, AI, or a combination

agent_name.description: AI agent assigned to this role (e.g., 'eos-ceo', 'eos-sales')

permission_tier.description: Role-level authority ceiling. One of: read, draft, execute, commit

responsibilities.description: What this role is accountable for (e.g., ['Pipeline management', 'Outreach strategy'])

workflows.description: Workflow slugs this role participates in

metrics.description: KPI slugs this role is measured on

tools.description: Tool identifiers this role has access to

documents.description: Document types/categories this role produces or consumes

dashboard_id.description: Dashboard configuration assigned to this role

autonomy_level.description: How much independent authority this role has (0=none, 5=full autonomy)

active.description: Whether the role is currently active

metadata.description: Extensible metadata bag for role-specific config

human_or_ai.description: OperatorType enum governs who fills the role. This is a first-class field, not a tag.

values.HUMAN: Role operated exclusively by a human team member
values.AI: Role operated exclusively by an AI agent. The agent_name field identifies which agent.
values.HYBRID: Role can be operated by either human or AI depending on context. The system supports hot-swapping between human and AI for hybrid roles.

permissions.description: Role permission_tier determines what actions the role holder can perform. Tiers are cumulative — each higher tier includes all lower capabilities.
permissions.enforcement: DepartmentAgent.execute_skill() checks PERMISSION_TIER.permits(skill.min_tier) before execution. Skills that require a tier above the agent's ceiling are rejected.

capabilities.description: Role capabilities are expressed through the skills registered on the corresponding DepartmentAgent. Each skill has a name, action_type, description, handler function, and minimum tier.
capabilities.tier_auto_mapping: If min_tier is not explicitly set, required_tier_for_action(action_type) determines it from TIER_ACTION_MAP
capabilities.browser_capabilities: Every DepartmentAgent gets browser_research (READ tier) and browser_act (EXECUTE tier) auto-registered

levels.name: Operator/User
levels.description: The human principal who owns and governs the entire system. Ultimate authority. All governance chains terminate here.
levels.cardinality: One operator per instance (MVP). Multi-operator at scale.

levels.name: Portfolio
levels.description: Strategic container grouping related entities. Provides consolidated dashboards, cross-entity analytics, capital allocation views.
levels.cardinality: One operator owns one or more portfolios. MVP: one primary portfolio.

levels.name: Company/Entity
levels.description: An operating business instance within a portfolio. Parent entity owning departments, BIS, knowledge graph, interactions. Maps to a venture in the database.
levels.cardinality: One portfolio contains one or more companies/entities.

levels.name: Department
levels.description: Structural grouping within a company owning roles, metrics, workflows, and an AI agent.
levels.cardinality: One company has 10 default departments. Custom departments can be added.

levels.name: Role
levels.description: The atomic operating unit. Everything attaches to a role. Operated by human, AI, or both.
levels.cardinality: One department has one or more roles.

levels.name: Workflow
levels.description: A repeatable process with triggers, steps, governance gates, and output artifacts.
levels.cardinality: One department owns one or more workflows.

levels.name: Dashboard
levels.description: The complete UI surface for a role/department with task board, tools, CRM, documents, workflows, metrics, communications, AI panel, and approval queue.
levels.cardinality: One per department (default). Role-specific overrides possible.

reporting_lines.description: Reporting follows the communication delegation architecture. Department agents report to CEO agent, CEO reports to EA (which surfaces to operator).
reporting_lines.chain: DepartmentAgent -> CEO Agent -> EA Agent -> Operator
reporting_lines.constraint: EA never routes directly to department agents. All department-level delegation flows through CEO.

delegation_rules.downward_delegation: CEO agent delegates to department agents with context, constraints, and deadline. Department agents execute within their permission tier.
delegation_rules.upward_escalation: Department agents escalate to CEO when action requires higher tier, business judgment needed, cross-department dependency, or risk exceeds authority.
delegation_rules.cross_department: CEO coordinates cross-department tasks by creating sub-tasks for each department with explicit dependency tracking.
delegation_rules.parallel_execution: Independent sub-tasks across departments are delegated in parallel. Dependent sub-tasks are sequenced.

template_system.description: Business type templates pre-configure the org chart with departments, roles, metrics, and workflows appropriate for that business type. Templates are the bridge between the abstract org chart engine and the specific reality of a founder's business.

business_type_templates.concept: Each business type in the ontology (19 types defined in phase14_6b_eos_portfolio_entity_business_ontology.json) gets a template that specifies which departments are active, which roles are emphasized, which metrics are primary, and which workflows are auto-provisioned.

template_structure.active_departments: Subset of 10 default departments to activate on creation
template_structure.primary_departments: Which departments are most critical for this business type (shown first, more prominent in UI)
template_structure.deferred_departments: Departments that exist but are dormant until the business reaches a certain stage
template_structure.custom_metrics: Business-type-specific KPIs layered on top of department defaults
template_structure.custom_workflows: Business-type-specific workflows layered on top of department defaults
template_structure.stage_gates: What triggers department activation or role expansion at each business stage

business_type_templates.note: Full 19-type template library is an implementation task. The 3 examples above demonstrate the pattern. Templates are not yet implemented in code.

customization_rules.description: Rules governing how operators can customize the org chart beyond templates.
allowed_customizations: Rename departments (display_name only, slug remains stable for code references)
Add custom roles within existing departments
Add custom metrics to any department
Add custom workflows to any department
Change department permission tiers (with governance warning if lowering)
Add custom departments beyond the default 10
prohibited_customizations: Cannot change department slug after creation (breaks code references and agent mapping)
Cannot remove the executive department (CEO is always required)
Cannot set a department tier higher than COMMIT
Cannot remove governance gates from workflows (can add, never remove)
Cannot create a role without a department parent
customization_rules.governance: Any customization that changes permission tiers, removes departments, or modifies workflow governance gates triggers a risk notice in the UI and requires explicit operator confirmation.

department_to_agent.description: Each department maps to exactly one DepartmentAgent subclass. The agent_name field on the Department model is the lookup key. Agent classes are registered in projections/eos/agents/.

features: Skill registration via _add_skill(name, action_type, description, handler, min_tier)
Permission tier enforcement via PermissionTier.permits() check before execution
Tier-gated action execution — skills that require a higher tier than the agent's ceiling are rejected
Browser research and browser act skills auto-registered on every agent instance
Org/venture context awareness via _org_id and _venture_id constructor params
Metadata export via metadata() method returning projection, department, tier, skill_count, skill list

capability_routing.description: How the system determines which department agent handles a given task. This is the CEO agent's delegation logic.
capability_routing.routing_method: CEO agent classifies incoming tasks by domain using skill/capability matching against department agent skill registries.
routing_signals: Action type requested (e.g., 'draft_message' -> check which departments have skills with that action_type)
Domain keywords in task description (e.g., 'revenue', 'expense' -> finance)
Explicit department reference in task (e.g., 'ask sales to...')
capability_routing.ambiguity_resolution: When a task could belong to multiple departments, CEO agent checks: (1) which department's metrics are most affected, (2) which department's workflows most closely match, (3) which department's permission tier is appropriate for the action. If still ambiguous, CEO coordinates a multi-department response.

tiers.description: Four-tier cumulative permission model. Each higher tier includes all lower capabilities.

tier_definitions.description: Read-only access. Can analyze, research, score, classify, summarize, query, report, and browse.
Can create drafts and artifacts but cannot send or execute. Includes all READ capabilities.
Can send messages, publish content, execute workflows, and interact with external systems. Includes all DRAFT and READ capabilities.

Can execute payments, sign contracts, approve actions, and make irreversible changes. Includes all EXECUTE, DRAFT, and READ capabilities. Reserved for departments where errors have financial or legal consequences.

rbac_abac_hybrid.description: EOS uses a hybrid RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) + ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) permission model.

rbac_layer.description: Roles define the base permission set. A user/agent's role determines their default tier and the actions they can perform.
rbac_layer.implementation: Role.permission_tier field sets the ceiling. DepartmentAgent.PERMISSION_TIER enforces at execution time.
rbac_layer.assignment: Roles are assigned during org setup (default_roles factory) or manually by the operator.

abac_layer.description: Attribute-based rules can override or refine role-based permissions based on context: business stage, risk level, time of day, financial thresholds, etc.
planned_attributes: business_stage: early-stage businesses may restrict COMMIT actions to operator-only
risk_level: HIGH/CRITICAL risk actions require explicit approval regardless of role tier
financial_threshold: actions above a configurable dollar amount require COMMIT tier + operator approval
time_context: after-hours actions may be restricted or queued for review
entity_context: different entities within a portfolio may have different permission policies
abac_layer.current_status: ABAC layer is architecturally planned but not yet implemented. Current enforcement is pure RBAC via PermissionTier.

what_ships_first.description: MVP org chart capabilities for R1-R2 (Core Shell + AI Foundation).
what_ships_first.departments: All 10 default departments ship in MVP. Template system activates the relevant subset based on business type.
what_ships_first.roles: One default role per department ships in MVP (from default_roles factory). Custom roles deferred.
what_ships_first.agents: All 10 implemented DepartmentAgent subclasses ship. EA Agent and Portfolio Advisor are critical gaps for R2+.
what_ships_first.permissions: 4-tier PermissionTier enforcement ships in MVP. ABAC layer deferred.
what_ships_first.dashboards: Default department dashboards with standard widget layouts ship in MVP.
what_ships_first.workflows: 10 default workflows (one per department) ship in MVP.
what_ships_first.templates: Business type templates for initial validation types (AI automation agency, coaching/info-product, SaaS) ship in MVP. Remaining 16 types are R3+.
what_ships_first.customization: Department activation/deactivation and role operator_type changes ship in MVP. Full customization deferred.
what_ships_first.multi_entity: Single entity per portfolio in MVP. Data model supports multiple but UI/agent coordination is single-entity.

what_deferred: EA Agent implementation (critical for corrected routing chain)
Portfolio Advisor Agent implementation (critical for multi-entity)
6 additional department agents (admin, research, content, automation, investment_analyst, asset_manager, property_manager)
Custom role creation with fine-grained permissions
Department template library for all 19 business types
Org chart evolution tracking (what changed, when, why)
Role autonomy_level enforcement (currently defined but not mechanically enforced)

auto_generation.description: End-state org chart generation is fully automated based on business type, stage, and operator preferences.
flow: Operator creates a new entity and selects business type
Template engine provisions the complete org chart: departments, roles, agents, workflows, metrics, dashboards
System activates departments appropriate for the current business stage
As the business grows (detected via KPI thresholds), system recommends activating deferred departments
AI agents auto-configure their skill emphasis based on the business's current binding constraint

evolution.description: End-state org charts evolve as the business grows. The system tracks org chart mutations as a versioned history.
capabilities: Stage-gated department activation: system detects business stage transitions and recommends new departments
Role creation recommendations: as workload increases, system suggests splitting roles or adding specialists
Metric evolution: as the business matures, KPIs shift from leading indicators (pipeline, outreach) to lagging indicators (NRR, LTV)
Workflow optimization: system analyzes workflow execution data and recommends improvements, parallelization, or automation upgrades
Agent skill tuning: based on execution feedback, agents emphasize skills that produce better outcomes for this specific business
Org chart versioning: every mutation is tracked with timestamp, reason, and before/after state

cross_entity.description: End-state supports cross-entity org chart intelligence within a portfolio.
capabilities: Shared roles: a single human (e.g., founder as CEO) can hold roles across multiple entities with entity-scoped context switching
Shared agents: certain agents (e.g., finance) can serve multiple entities within a portfolio with entity-specific configuration
Cross-entity benchmarking: compare org chart configurations, staffing levels, and efficiency across entities
Portfolio-level org view: aggregated view of all departments, roles, and agents across all entities in a portfolio
Resource sharing recommendations: system identifies where entities could share resources (e.g., one legal agent serving 3 entities)

open_questions.question: Should department agents be instantiated per-entity or shared across entities with entity context passed per-call?
open_questions.rationale: Per-entity instances enable entity-specific memory and configuration but increase resource usage. Shared instances are lighter but risk context bleeding between entities.
open_questions.recommendation: Per-entity instances for MVP (simpler, safer). Consider shared-with-isolation for scale.

open_questions.question: Should custom departments be fully user-defined or constrained to a curated extension library?
open_questions.rationale: Fully user-defined departments require dynamic agent creation which is significantly more complex. A curated library (the 6 planned additional departments plus a small set of industry-specific ones) covers most use cases with much less complexity.

open_questions.question: How should the org chart handle business type changes (e.g., agency pivots to SaaS)?
open_questions.rationale: A pivot changes which departments are primary, which metrics matter, and which workflows are active. The system needs a migration path that preserves existing data and agent memory while re-configuring the org chart for the new business type.

open_questions.question: Should the autonomy_level field on Role (0-5 scale) be enforced mechanically or remain advisory?
open_questions.rationale: Currently defined on the Role model (default=2) but not mechanically enforced anywhere. Enforcement would mean: level 0 = every action requires approval, level 5 = agent acts autonomously. This is a significant governance decision.

open_questions.question: Should the SKILL_ALLOCATION map in entities.py be the canonical skill-to-department assignment, or should skills self-register their department affinity?
open_questions.rationale: Current SKILL_ALLOCATION is a static dict mapping department slugs to skill paths. Some departments have 0 skills allocated (finance, hr, legal, product). Self-registration would let skills declare their department affinity, but centralized allocation gives the operator explicit control.

open_questions.question: How should the permission model handle temporary permission elevation (e.g., operator grants a DRAFT-tier agent temporary EXECUTE access for a specific task)?
open_questions.rationale: Current PermissionTier is static per agent. Temporary elevation is a common real-world need (e.g., product manager needs to deploy a hotfix). Requires scoped, time-limited, audited permission grants.

implementation_debt.description: CEO agent strategic_analysis skill contains hardcoded instance-specific references (Initiate Arena business context). Must be generalized to use BIS runtime lookup for multi-entity support.
implementation_debt.resolution: Replace hardcoded references with BIS venture registry lookup. Agent should load business context dynamically from org_id + venture_id.

implementation_debt.description: SKILL_ALLOCATION map has empty lists for 4 departments (finance, hr, legal, product). These departments have agent skills but no allocated external skill paths.
implementation_debt.resolution: Either populate with relevant skill paths as they are created, or migrate to self-registration where skills declare their department affinity.

implementation_debt.description: Role autonomy_level field (0-5) is defined on the model but not mechanically enforced by DepartmentAgent execution. It is purely advisory.
implementation_debt.resolution: Decide whether to enforce mechanically (OQ-ORG-004) or remove to avoid misleading the data model.

implementation_debt.description: No inter-agent communication infrastructure exists. DepartmentAgent instances are standalone classes with no message passing, delegation protocol, or routing logic between them. The routing chain (EA -> CEO -> Department) is architecturally defined but not mechanically implemented.
implementation_debt.resolution: Implement inter-agent message passing using the substrate signal infrastructure (SignalEnvelope routing). CEO agent needs a delegation method that creates tasks for department agents and monitors completion.

implementation_debt.description: EA Agent and Portfolio Advisor Agent do not exist in code. These are critical nodes in the corrected communication routing chain.
implementation_debt.resolution: Implement EA Agent (may need a distinct base class from DepartmentAgent since it routes rather than executes) and Portfolio Advisor Agent. See phase14_6b_eos_communication_delegation_architecture.json for full spec.

implementation_debt.description: Business type template system is architecturally defined but not implemented. No code exists to provision org charts from business type selection.
implementation_debt.resolution: Implement template registry (JSON or Python dict) mapping business types to department configurations. Wire into onboarding flow so entity creation auto-provisions the org chart.

implementation_debt.description: Dashboard widget configurations are defined in entities.py::default_dashboards() but not wired to the SaaS frontend. The dashboards exist as Pydantic models but do not render in the UI.
implementation_debt.resolution: Wire Dashboard model serialization to the SaaS API layer. Frontend needs to consume DashboardWidget configs and render the appropriate widget components.

implementation_debt.description: Default workflows in entities.py define full step sequences with trigger types, execution modes, and approval gates, but no workflow execution engine exists to run them.
implementation_debt.resolution: Implement workflow execution engine that interprets Workflow/WorkflowStep models, manages state transitions, enforces approval gates, and triggers actions through DepartmentAgent skill execution.
